1.title: Integration, Developer Tools and Other Services
1.text: Welcome to Module twelve: Integration, Developer Tools and Other Services. This module covers task statement three point eight, the remaining service categories in the exam guide: application integration, business applications, developer tools, end-user computing, frontend and mobile, and the Internet of Things. Each service here has a clear, single purpose, so the exam asks you to match a need to a name.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do five things. Choose between Amazon S Q S, Amazon S N S, Amazon EventBridge and A W S Step Functions. Place Amazon Connect and Amazon S E S among business applications. Say what A W S CodeBuild, A W S CodePipeline and A W S X-Ray do for developers. Tell WorkSpaces, WorkSpaces Applications and WorkSpaces Secure Browser apart. And recognize A W S Amplify for web and mobile, and A W S I o T Core for devices.

1.title: Case Check-In: Tidewater's Order Day
1.text: It is order day at Tidewater. A placed order must reach fulfillment, send an email, and text the warehouse, all at once. A support team takes calls and chats, and the shop sends order confirmation emails. Developers want every code change built, tested and released automatically. Warehouse staff need a Windows application on any device, and fridge sensors must report temperatures. Your job is to choose the service for each of these needs.

1.title: Queues and Topics: Amazon SQS and Amazon SNS
1.text: Two messaging services look similar, so learn the difference. Amazon Simple Queue Service, or S Q S, is a hosted queue that decouples components. Producers send messages, and consumers process them later, so messages wait until they are processed. Standard queues deliver at least once, and first-in first-out queues process exactly once. Messages are kept four days by default, and up to fourteen. Amazon Simple Notification Service, or S N S, is publish and subscribe. One message to a topic reaches every subscriber, including S Q S queues, Lambda, H T T P S endpoints, email, mobile push and S M S. In the figure, the shop publishes one order, and S N S fans it out to a queue, an email address and a text message. Exam tip: one message to many subscribers means S N S; messages waiting for a consumer mean S Q S.

1.title: Events and Workflows: Amazon EventBridge and AWS Step Functions
1.text: Two more integration services appear. Amazon EventBridge is a serverless event bus. It connects application components with events from A W S services, your own applications and software-as-a-service partners. Rules route events to targets, Pipes link one source to one target, and Scheduler runs tasks on a schedule. Think of it as reacting to events. A W S Step Functions provides serverless workflows, called state machines, that orchestrate Lambda and other services. They are visual to build and debug, and they can retry and catch errors. Standard workflows run up to a year, and Express workflows run up to five minutes. Think of it as coordinating steps. Exam tip: routing events and scheduling tasks mean EventBridge; coordinating a multi-step process means Step Functions.

1.title: Business Applications: Amazon Connect and Amazon SES
1.text: Two services cover business applications. Amazon Connect is a cloud contact center. Customers reach agents by voice, chat or S M S, with intelligent routing and real-time metrics. A W S now calls the product Amazon Connect Customer, and the name Amazon Connect covers a wider set of agentic A I solutions, so older material uses the earlier name. You pay only for what you use, with no contact center hardware to run. Amazon S E S, the Simple Email Service, sends and receives email with your own addresses and domains. Use it for transactional email, such as order confirmations, and for marketing email and newsletters. You pay by the volume sent and received. Exam tip: a cloud contact center means Amazon Connect; sending application email means Amazon S E S.

1.title: Developer Tools: CodeBuild, CodePipeline and X-Ray
1.text: Three developer tools are in scope. A W S CodeBuild is a fully managed build service. It compiles code, runs unit tests and produces deployable artifacts, with no build servers to manage, and you are billed by build minutes. A W S CodePipeline is continuous delivery. It models, visualizes and automates the steps that release your software. In the figure, a change moves through source, build and test, and deploy stages, and CodeBuild can be the build or test action inside the pipeline. A W S X-Ray collects data about requests, and its trace map shows bottlenecks, latency spikes and errors across services. Exam tip: build and test means CodeBuild; automate releases means CodePipeline; trace and troubleshoot mean X-Ray.

1.title: End-User Computing: WorkSpaces, WorkSpaces Applications and Secure Browser
1.text: Three services put applications and desktops in front of end users. Amazon WorkSpaces provides virtual, cloud-based desktops, running Windows or Linux. WorkSpaces Personal is persistent, WorkSpaces Pools are non-persistent, and users reach them from many devices. Think of a whole desktop. Amazon WorkSpaces Applications, earlier called Amazon AppStream two point zero, streams desktop applications from A W S to a client or browser, and data is never stored on the device. Think of one application. Amazon WorkSpaces Secure Browser, earlier called WorkSpaces Web, is a secure browser for internal websites and software-as-a-service apps, in an isolated environment, with no data on the device and no V P N. Think of a safe browser. As of the fourth of November, twenty twenty-six, A W S closed Secure Browser to new customers on the twenty-ninth of October, twenty twenty-six, but the exam guide still lists it. Exam tip: a desktop means WorkSpaces; one streamed application means WorkSpaces Applications; a secure browser means Secure Browser.

1.title: Web, Mobile and Devices: AWS Amplify and AWS IoT Core
1.text: Two last services cover web, mobile and devices. A W S Amplify gives frontend web and mobile developers tools to build and host applications on A W S. Amplify Hosting offers a Git-based workflow with continuous deployment for full-stack serverless web apps, delivered through the A W S content delivery network. Its features include feature branches, custom domains, pull request previews and atomic deployments. A W S I o T Core connects Internet of Things devices to A W S services and to each other. Its message broker supports M Q T T and H T T P S, and A W S I o T Core for Lo Ra W A N manages low-power wide-area devices. Exam tip: frontend and mobile apps mean Amplify; connecting and managing devices means I o T Core.

1.title: What the Exam Asks: Other Services
1.text: Here is how the exam frames this module. S Q S or S N S: messages wait in a queue, or one message goes to many subscribers. EventBridge or Step Functions: route events and schedules, or coordinate a workflow. Connect or S E S: a cloud contact center, or application email. CodeBuild, CodePipeline or X-Ray: build and test, automate releases, or trace requests. WorkSpaces, WorkSpaces Applications or Secure Browser: a desktop, one application, or a safe browser. Amplify or I o T Core: web and mobile apps, or devices. And A W S Support covers the support plans you can add, which Module fourteen explains. Exam tip: name the need, then the service.

1.title: Design Check: Tidewater's Order Day
1.text: Now a design check. Cover the right column and answer each row yourself. One order message to fulfillment, email and S M S: Amazon S N S, with S Q S queues. Orders wait safely until servers can process them: Amazon S Q S. A multi-step refund process with retries: A W S Step Functions. A support team taking calls and chats: Amazon Connect. Order confirmation emails: Amazon S E S. Every code change built, tested and released: CodeBuild and CodePipeline. Find the slow call inside the shop: A W S X-Ray. A Windows application on any device: WorkSpaces Applications. A new storefront web app, hosted with continuous deployment: A W S Amplify. And fridge sensors reporting temperatures: A W S I o T Core. Pause the video if you want more time.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. For messaging, S Q S queues messages, S N S fans one message out, EventBridge routes events, and Step Functions coordinates workflows. For business applications, Amazon Connect is a cloud contact center, and Amazon S E S sends email. For developer tools, CodeBuild builds and tests, CodePipeline automates releases, and X-Ray traces requests. For end-user computing, WorkSpaces gives desktops, WorkSpaces Applications streams apps, and Secure Browser gives safe browsing. And for web, mobile and devices, Amplify serves frontend and mobile apps, and I o T Core connects devices.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. When Tidewater's shop takes an order, the same message must reach fulfillment and also trigger an email and a text message to the warehouse. Which service sends one message to many subscribers? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B, Amazon S N S. It publishes a message to a topic, and every subscriber, such as a queue, an email address or a phone number, receives a copy. S Q S holds messages for a consumer, Step Functions coordinates workflow steps, and X-Ray traces requests.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. The shop's web servers sometimes send order messages faster than the processing servers can handle them. Which service lets the orders wait safely until a consumer processes them? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C, Amazon S Q S. It is a hosted queue that decouples components, so messages wait until a consumer processes them. S N S pushes messages to subscribers, S E S sends email, and I o T Core connects devices.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. Select two. Tidewater's developers want every code change built, tested and released through automated stages. Which two services help? The five options are on the screen. The answers are A and B. CodeBuild compiles code, runs tests and produces artifacts, and CodePipeline automates the stages that release them. WorkSpaces provides desktops, X-Ray traces requests in a running application, and Connect is a contact center.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. Tidewater wants warehouse staff to stream a Windows desktop application from A W S to their devices, with no data stored on those devices. Which service fits best? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D, Amazon WorkSpaces Applications, formerly Amazon AppStream two point zero. It streams desktop applications from A W S, and the data is never stored on the user's device. Amplify hosts web apps, Connect Customer is a contact center, and I o T Core connects devices.

1.title: Answers at a Glance
1.text: Here are all four answers. Question one: B. Question two: C. Question three: A and B. Question four: D. That completes Module twelve, and with it the technology domain. Next, Module thirteen opens the last domain: pricing models and cost management.
